text:
Lena Park: hi all, starting my first week! I followed the "getting-started" steps but `kubectl config get-contexts` shows only a bare default context. I expected redwood-dev. I need a namespace (lena-dev) to test port-forwarding. who handles kube onboarding?

Samir Patel: welcome Lena :wave: @devops usually handles RBAC/namespace creation but we can sort quick. Are you able to authenticate via Okta? `kubectl auth can-i get pods` should show yes/no.

Lena Park: I ran `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n lena-dev` and got: "error: You must be logged in to the server (the server has asked for the client to provide credentials)". I did complete Okta SSO and enrolled my device yesterday.

Ivy Chen: hmm that error usually means the kubeconfig doesn't have the Okta exec plugin entry. Can you paste the contexts portion of `kubectl config view --raw` (sanitized)?

Lena Park: sanitized output:
```
contexts:
- context:
    cluster: redwood-dev
    user: lena@redwood.ai
  name: redwood-dev
```

Lena Park: user looks fine?

Samir Patel: the user looks like an email rather than the Okta exec user format. Our Okta integration uses `okta:email@domain`. Might be the login step didn't complete. Try `okta login` (we have an internal wrapper) or run the SSO flow: `redwood-sso login --okta`

Lena Park: running `redwood-sso login --okta` now... it opens the browser, I auth, it returns a code and then nothing changes in terminal. `kubectl get namespaces` still errors with same message.

Ivy Chen: sometimes the id-token isn't written to kubeconfig because the connector needs a directory sync. @onboard-bot can you trigger a directory sync for lena@redwood.ai?

onboard-bot: Directory sync queued for lena@redwood.ai (job id sync-2026-07-01-42). Estimated time ~30s.

infra-bot: FYI: There was a recent change to the Okta-to-k8s mapping; if a sync is required the error will show as: "cannot list resource \"namespaces\"" or the auth error you saw.

Samir Patel: while we wait, Lena can you try `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev` then `kubectl config view --minify --raw` and check the user entry. If it still shows `lena@redwood.ai`, try running `redwood-sso doctor` to surface errors.

Lena Park: did that: user still `lena@redwood.ai`. `redwood-sso doctor` output: "okta-client: token not present in kubeconfig; last-login: 2026-07-01T09:12:03Z".

Ivy Chen: looks like the client didn't write the exec plugin block. Samir, can you create the namespace and a RoleBinding granting `edit` to the Okta principal once the sync completes? Name: lena-dev, rb: rb-lena-dev-edit.

Samir Patel: on it. Will wait for sync to finish then apply.

onboard-bot: Directory sync completed for lena@redwood.ai (job id sync-2026-07-01-42). Mapping refreshed.

Lena Park: re-ran `redwood-sso login --okta` and now `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n lena-dev` -> "no" (expected until RBAC applied).

Samir Patel: created namespace `lena-dev` and RoleBinding `rb-lena-dev-edit` binding `edit` to `okta:lena@redwood.ai`. Applied. Give it a moment to propagate.

Lena Park: `kubectl get pods -n lena-dev` -> no resources found. success! set default ns: `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=lena-dev`. port-forward works to my dev service. :thumbsup:

Ivy Chen: awesome. I'll add a note in the onboarding doc: run `redwood-sso doctor` if `kubectl` still complains after SSO. Also mention the possible 30-60s delay for directory sync.

Lena Park: thank you everyone! one follow-up: where do I request a service account for CI?

Samir Patel: open a ticket in #eng-infra with the name and verbs. We prefer namespaced service accounts for dev work.

Lena Park: perfect. excited to get started :smile:
